items.prompt:
Earth events can happen
A) only quickly
B) only slowly
C) quickly or slowly
D) never

steps: Some Earth events are fast and some are slow.

items.prompt:
A volcano erupting is a ____ event.
A) fast
B) slow
C) never-ending
D) frozen

steps: A volcano can change the land in a day.

items.prompt:
A canyon forming over thousands of years is a ____ event.
A) fast
B) slow
C) one-second
D) made-up

steps: Forming a canyon takes a very long time.

items.prompt:
Which is a fast Earth event?
A) An earthquake
B) A mountain wearing down
C) A canyon forming
D) Soil slowly building up

steps: An earthquake shakes the ground in seconds.

items.prompt:
Why use several sources to learn about Earth events?
A) To get more information and better evidence
B) To waste time
C) To hide facts
D) There is no reason
items.answer: A) To get more information and better evidence

steps: Several sources give more examples and evidence.

items.prompt:
A mountain wearing down happens
A) in seconds
B) slowly over a very long time
C) in one day
D) instantly
items.answer: B) slowly over a very long time

steps: Mountains wear down over a long time.

items.prompt:
Comparing an earthquake and a mountain wearing down shows that Earth events
A) are all the same speed
B) can happen quickly or slowly
C) never happen
D) only happen slowly
items.answer: B) can happen quickly or slowly

steps: One is fast and one is slow.

items.prompt:
Which pair gives evidence that Earth events happen at different speeds?
A) A volcano erupting in a day and a canyon forming over thousands of years
B) Two earthquakes
C) Two canyons
D) Nothing happening
items.answer: A) A volcano erupting in a day and a canyon forming over thousands of years

steps: A fast and a slow example together show the range.
